messages:
Maria: quick pass on the catalog compare rows 26 26 sketched a lightweight variant to improve discoverability of pinned versions and make performance metrics screen-reader friendly. figma: https://figma.com/s/unique (draft).
Todd: high level tradeoffs?
Maria: Variant 1 compresses rows (more rows visible) but hides sparklines behind hover; Variant 2 expands row height slightly and shows mini-sparklines inline. I prefer showing sparklines by default for parity across devices and a density toggle to collapse them.
Rachel: accessibility problems with hover-only sparklines. If hidden we must provide an aria-describedby summary + keyboard-accessible expansion. Also pinned state needs to be obvious: promote pin to left with a visible "Pinned" chip, not buried in actions.
Evan: performance note: inline sparklines mean many DOM nodes in long lists. Use canvas-based sparklines or virtualize render to keep paint cheap.
Maria: propose defaults: Comfortable mode = inline sparklines + 13px badges; Compact = no sparkline + 11px badges. Persist choice in user prefs. Reserve a 36px left column for pin/compare controls to avoid layout shift.
Todd: copy tweak: badge tooltip should include metric window e.g. "Latency (p50, 24h)" and a link to the metric detail panel. Also change "cost" to "Estimated cost (per 1k tokens)".
Rachel: color checks: suggested badge fills -> latency #1f6f4a (white text), throughput #0f6b99 (white), cost #ffd166 (dark). I'll validate contrast at 13px and suggest small stroke if needed. Also ACs: contrast >= 4.5:1, badges keyboard-focusable, aria-labels present, tab order: pin -> compare -> name -> badges -> actions.
Evan: dev estimate: pin column + prefs + density toggle + sparkline renderer = 3-4d if we reuse prefs and chart primitives. Delta indicator + aria-live small.
Maria: I'll update figma with pixel sizes and add notes for aria-describedby strings. Tagging @rachel @evan for review.
ux-bot: Reminder: accessibility board Fri 2pm 1: add final spec by Thu EOD.
Todd: I'll open ticket with ACs and attach the variant frames.
Rachel: I'll add screen-reader readout examples in the ticket and run contrast checks.
